title: When a log line becomes an error report

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A log line says something happened. But to fix an error, you also need the exception, the release, the environment and what the request looked like. How do you get both in one place?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'd guess you wire your logging to your error tracker.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly, and that's Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK, a .NET package from Antoine. It's based on an existing sink from the Serilog community, and it connects Serilog logging to Sentry error reporting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's a sink, in this world?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The place logs flow into. Think of Serilog as a river of log events, and a sink as a channel that carries them somewhere. Here, the channel leads to Sentry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The sink receives each log event and hands it to a small wrapper around the Sentry SDK. The wrapper covers three jobs: capturing messages, capturing exceptions, and creating transactions. Because that boundary is small, it's easy to swap out in tests.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The sink starts Sentry itself, so you decide once who owns initialization, and it needs a real D S N. Install it with dotnet add package, and the repo has console and ASP.NET Core demos to copy from.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A companion project brings request context. It has a request adapter, a destructuring policy, exception extensions and middleware, so errors arrive with the details that help you investigate.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. There are advanced options and a beforeSend callback to filter or enrich events, and the code documents how that fits with the sink's own event mapping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two main packages target net6 and net10, plus separate variants for each. A live NuGet badge shows the download count.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The README documents xUnit tests, coverage collection and formatting checks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So logs and errors finally tell one story. The full write-up has the diagram of the adapter.
